late: Assessment Policy: Late Work and Extensions (synthetic teaching text). Every assignment has a published deadline that is shown on the course page and repeated in the first lecture. Late submission is normally penalized. Illness extensions require medical evidence before the deadline. The penalty is five marks for each day after the deadline, and work that arrives more than seven days late is not marked unless the examinations office has approved a longer arrangement for reasons that were reported in writing to the course coordinator, for example a long hospital stay, a bereavement in the immediate family, or a documented technical failure of the learning portal that affected every student in the course. Students who expect to miss a deadline should contact the course coordinator, Dr. Rana, as early as possible, e.g. during the first week of the assignment, and should keep copies of every message. A request made after the deadline has passed is treated as a late submission. Group work follows the same rules, and each member must confirm the request. Extensions apply only to the assignment named in the request and do not move the dates of other assessments. Approved extensions are recorded in the student record and reported to the department at the end of the term.
password: IT Help: Student Accounts and Passwords (synthetic teaching text). Every student receives a university account on the first day of enrolment, and the account gives access to email, the learning portal and the wireless network. Reset a forgotten password using the recovery link. Never share recovery codes. The recovery link is shown on the login page below the sign-in button and is sent to the personal email address that was registered at enrolment, so students should keep that address current. A recovery link stays valid for thirty minutes, and after three failed attempts the account is locked for one hour to protect it from guessing. If the personal address is no longer available, a student may visit the IT service desk in Building B with a student card, where staff can verify identity and update the address. The service desk will not tell anyone a password, and it will not reset a password on behalf of another person, even a classmate or a family member. Passwords must contain at least twelve characters. Students should not reuse a password from another service. Report any suspicious message that asks for a recovery code to the security team, because genuine staff never ask for one.
assignment: Coursework Submission Guide (synthetic teaching text). This guide explains how students hand in written work for taught modules. Upload assignments through the learning portal. Submit the final file as a PDF. Open the course page, select the assignment, attach the file and press the submit button, then keep the confirmation receipt that the portal displays. The portal accepts files up to twenty megabytes, and a file with a different format, such as a word-processor document or an image, is rejected with a warning message. Lab reports are different: submit lab reports by email to the lab coordinator, and do not use the learning portal for them, because lab reports are marked on paper at the end of each practical session. If the portal is unavailable before a deadline, take a screenshot of the error message and email it to the course coordinator at once, which allows the coordinator to record that a technical problem occurred and to accept the file by an alternative route if that is appropriate. Late uploads are handled under the assessment policy. Keep a copy of every submitted file until the final marks have been published. Do not include your name in the file name unless the instructions ask for it.
contractor: Workplace Policy: Remote Work (synthetic teaching text). This policy sets out who may work away from the office and what conditions apply. Employees may work remotely for up to two days each week with the approval of their line manager, and the arrangement is reviewed every six months. Contractors can work remotely only if the signed contract permits it. Employee rules do not apply to contractors. A contractor whose contract is silent on remote work must work on site until the contract is amended in writing by the contracting office. Managers should not promise remote work to a contractor by email or in conversation, because only the signed contract counts, and a verbal promise does not change the terms. All remote workers must use the managed laptop supplied by the university and must connect through the approved virtual private network when they open internal systems. Equipment must be returned when the arrangement ends. Questions about eligibility should be sent to the human resources office, which keeps the current version of this policy and the date on which each version took effect. This version replaces earlier versions.
printer: Equipment Troubleshooting: Printers and Scanners (synthetic teaching text). Technicians should read the warning before following any procedure. Switch the device off and unplug it before opening any cover, because the fuser unit can stay hot for several minutes. For blank printer pages, check ink levels and run the cleaning utility. Print a test page afterwards. If the pages are still blank after two cleaning cycles, replace the cartridge and repeat the test page, and record the cartridge serial number on the service sheet so that repeated failures of one batch can be noticed by the stores team. A scanner behaves differently: for a blank scanner image, check document placement and select the correct scanning source, because a document placed face up on the glass produces a white image. Never use compressed air inside the printer, and do not touch the roller with bare fingers. Faults that continue after these steps must be reported to the equipment desk with the model name, the error code and the date. Follow the device manual for any step that is not listed here. Keep a log of each repair for audit purposes.
staff_it: IT Help: Staff Accounts (synthetic teaching text). Staff accounts are managed separately from student accounts and follow stricter rules. Staff reset a forgotten password by visiting the IT service desk in person with photo identification. The recovery link on the login page is disabled for staff accounts, so staff should not request one. A staff password must contain at least sixteen characters and must be changed every ninety days. After five failed sign-in attempts the account is locked until the service desk unlocks it, which normally takes less than an hour on weekdays. Staff who work off campus may ask the service desk to arrange a temporary access code by telephone, but only after the service desk has confirmed the identity of the caller using two pieces of information held in the personnel record. Shared accounts are not allowed, and a password must never be written on paper or stored in a document on a shared drive. Suspicious messages should be reported to the security team at once, together with the time at which the message arrived and the sender address that was shown.
